line: e4 e5 Bc4 Nf6 d3 Nc6 Nf3
teaches: Two different opening sequences that arrive at the same position are the same game, and an unfamiliar first move is nothing to fear once you see it landing in a structure you already understand — learn positions and plans, not move-order trivia. Recognising the transposition turns a strange start into familiar ground.
explains: With the bishop already posted on c4 and the modest d3 supporting the centre, the knight steps to f3 and reaches exactly the quiet, familiar centre that a more common move order arrives at from the other side. The knight eyes the e5-pawn and the position settles into well-known paths.
